fixture.tossResult: South Africa won the toss and elected to bat.

players.name: Aiden Markram
players.bio:
Aiden Markram is a talented opening batter from Northerns and he became the first South African captain to win a World Cup, albeit at under age level (2014 Under-19 World Cup).

He made his Test debut in 2017, falling just short of a century with 97 against Bangladesh in Potchefstroom. He first Test series against Australia was a raging success too, scoring two tons (143 and 152) as South Africa won the 2018 series 3-1.

Dropped from the Test side in 2022, Markram returned to the side in 2023 and cemented his spot with hundreds against West Indies and India.

Markram has captained his country in both white-ball formats and is a handy off-spinner and fielder.

players.name: Quinton de Kock
players.didyouKnow: Shares his record of four ODI centuries before the age of 21 with Irish cricketer Paul Stirling.
players.bio:
Quinton de Kock had achieved more by his 21st birthday than many cricketers do in their career.

The wicketkeeper has caused plenty of excitement not only for his skills behind the stumps, but for his considerable talent with the bat as well.

de Kock first made his mark on the South Africa Under-19 team, where he was a stand-out batsman, before he earned his first senior selection for the Proteas’ in a T20I clash with New Zealand in 2012.

A spot in South Africa’s one-day squad soon followed, and de Kock made a significant breakthrough with his first one-day international century against Pakistan in 2013.

The left-hander blazed his way to five centuries in his first 19 ODI appearances, becoming the first player to score three successive one-day centuries and the second player to score four ODI centuries before his 21st birthday.

de Kock made his Test debut for the Proteas and made three centuries in his first 15 matches.

As a result, de Kock has quickly become a household name not only in South Africa, but around the world.

players.name: Ryan Rickelton
players.bio:
A flashy left-handed batter, Ryan Rickelton was 25 when he made his Test debut against Bangladesh in 2022.

While it took him a couple of years to cement his place in the side, Rickelton was instrumental in South Africa's run to the 2023-25 WTC Final with scores of 101 against Sri Lanka and 259 against Pakistan in important victories.

A strong season for MI Cape Town in the SA20 league saw Rickelton earn an IPL contract with Mumbai Indians, scoring 388 in 2025.

players.name: David Miller
players.didyouKnow: Hit four sixes in his maiden first-class century, an unbeaten 108 for the Dolphins in 2009.
players.bio:
David Miller played hockey, tennis and squash as a boy, but it was cricket which captured the 25-year-old from Pietermaritzburg’s heart.

He made his debut in the Proteas’ one-day side at age of 20 in 2010, playing 13 matches in the lead-up to the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup. But his hopes of playing at the tournament were dashed when he missed out on selection in South Africa’s final squad.

The powerful hitter has also gained world recognition after explosive performances for Kings XI Punjab in the IPL in 2013.

Miller made his maiden international hundred against the West Indies and then two innings later, in the 2015 ICC World Cup he mad an unbeaten 138 against Zimbabwe.  

He has represented South Africa in ODI and T20 cricket but is yet to receive a Test match cap for the Proteas.

players.name: Tristan Stubbs
players.bio:
A tall wicketkeeper-batter who can hit the ball a mile, at 21 years of age Tristan Stubbs already had an IPL contract with Mumbai Indians before he'd made his international debut.

The right hander is particularly strong against spin and can hit to all areas of the ground with his long reach and inventive batting.

Having been a regular in the Proteas' T20 side, Stubbs made his Test debut in 2024 in an effort to add more firepower to SA's middle order and after a slow start against India and West Indies, Stubbs hit centuries against Bangladesh and Sri Lanka to highlight his supreme talents.

players.name: Marco Jansen
players.bio:
A left armer who can swing the ball both ways, Marco Jansen also stands at over 2m tall.

Jansen was only 21 when he made his Test debut and had his first Test five-wicket haul less than a year later when he claimed 5-35 against England at the Oval.

In late 2024 he took a barely believable 7-13 against Sri Lanka in Durban as the visitors were bowled out for 42.

Jansen is an all-format player for South Africa and is more than handy with the bat too, with multiple half-centuries already under his belt.

players.name: Kagiso Rabada
players.didyouKnow: Originally played rugby before switching to cricket.
players.bio:
Kagiso Rabada made his Proteas debut in a T20I against Australia in Adelaide at just 19.

Rabada was one of the stars of the South Africa team who won their maiden ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup in 2014, claiming 6-25 in the semi-final against Australia in a man-of-the-match performance.

The fast bowler made his first class debut in March 2014 and the selectors were quickly impressed, granting him a Test debut in 2015.

Adapting quickly to the highest level, Rabada took a seven-wicket haul in the first-innings against England at Centurion in just his fifth Test.

In his first Test series against Australia, the spearhead took 11-150 in the Gqeberha Test as South Africa won the match and levelled the series.

In 2024, Rabada became just the sixth South African to take 300 Test wickets, all while maintaining a strike rate below 40 and an average below 23.

players.name: Keshav Maharaj
players.bio:
Keshav Maharaj was rewarded with a Test debut for the Proteas after fantastic first-class form for the Dolphins.

His first match came in 2016 against Australia at the WACA. He had a great first game, taking 3-56 in the first-innings, which included the wicket of Steve Smith, and making 41 not out.

A crafty left-arm spinner, Maharaj's first Test in the subcontinent (2018) saw him take 9-129 against Sri Lanka before taking another three in the second innings.

He added his name to a select list when he took a hat-trick against West Indies in 2021.

In 2024 Maharaj became South Africa's most-prolific spinner in Test cricket, going past Hugh Tayfield's mark of 170 wickets in the format.

players.name: Lungi Ngidi
players.bio:
Lungi Ngidi's Test debut start in fine style in 2018 when the burly quick took 6-39 in India's second innings as South Africa won at Centurion.

Over the next few years he built an impressive Test record, which included a five-wicket haul in the West Indies and another six-wicket haul against India three years later.

Ngidi didn't play a Test in 2023 although he did feature for South Africa at the ODI World Cup that year, however groin and back injuries hampered the development of the exciting spearhead.

players.name: Hardik Pandya
players.bio:
Hardik Pandya made his international debut for India against Australia in 2016.

His ODI debut came later that year against New Zealand, while he made his Test debut in 2017 against Sri Lanka where he made a half-century in his first innings.

players.name: Washington Sundar
players.bio:
Hailing from Chennai in India’s south, Washington Sundar featured as a batting allrounder in the 2016 Under-19 World Cup as a 16-year-old.

The following year, Sundar made his IPL debut for Rising Pune Super Giants and his economical off-spin caught the eye.

By the end of 2017, his fast-tracked rise was complete, making his ODI and T20I debuts against Sri Lanka.

A really strong performance for Royal Challengers Bangalore in the 2020 IPL, where his economy rate was only 5.96 across 15 matches, helped earn him a call up to India’s Test squad that travelled to Australia at the end of the year.

Injury to fellow Tamil Nadu spinner Ravichandran Ashwin allow Sundar to make his Test debut in Brisbane in early 2021, a famous match where India chased a big fourth-innings total to secure the Border-Gavaskar Trophy.

Although he was consistently around the national T20 squad from 2019 onwards, Sundar was overlooked for the 20-over World Cups in 2021, 2022 and 2024.

The offie ended a three-and-a-half year absence from the Test team with his 7-59 against New Zealand in October 2024.

players.name: Arshdeep Singh
players.bio:
Arshdeep Singh made his international debut in a T20I against England in 2022.

The left-arm quick has been used as a white-ball specialist by India, with his speed and ability to consistently hit the yorker length deployed to good effect in the death overs regularly.

Arshdeep made a mark on the international stage instantly, achieving the rare feat of starting with a maiden over in his first-ever match.

He has since gone on to become first and the fastest Indian bowler to take 100 wickets in Men's T20Is.

A highlight of Arshdeep's career came at the MCG in 2022. Playing his first T20 World Cup game, a high-pressure encounter against arch-rivals Pakistan, the young fast bowler removed opposition captain Babar Azam on a golden duck with his very first ball. He followed it up with the wicket of the other opener, Mohammad Rizwan, in his next over.

The Punjab player finished as the leading wicket-taker for his team in that tournament. In the next edition of the T20 World Cup in 2024, he was the overall join-highest wicket taker for the tournament, taking 17 scalps. He was also named in the ICC Team of the Tournament.

Arshdeep is currently India's highest wicket-taker in Men’s T20Is, having overtaken Yuzvendra Chahal in 2025.

players.name: Jasprit Bumrah
players.didyouKnow: On Boxing Day 2018, Bumrah became the first Asian bowler to take five wickets in Australia, England and South Africa in the same calendar year.
players.bio:
Jasprit Bumrah is on all levels a unique bowler. With a lackadaisical approach to the wicket, sometimes off no more than six paces, Bumrah is renowned as one of the most lethal fast bowlers across formats.

Bumrah emerged in Australia in 2016 as a limited-overs talent making both his ODI and T20I debuts against Australia within the space of four days.

He was an immediate success, and after years of great results with Mumbai Indians in the IPL, the longest format beckoned for Bumrah.

After Steve Smith (ODI) and David Warner (T20) were his first wickets in white-ball internationals, he claimed the scalp of AB de Villiers for his first Test wicket in January 2018 and took another 47 more wickets in the year to come.

He followed that up with a memorable 2018-19 summer against Australia, taking career-best figures of 6-33 in the Boxing Day Test as India won the Border-Gavaskar Trophy on Aussie soil.


He became the first bowler from an Asian nation to take five-wicket hauls in Australia, England and South Africa in the same year.


In 2022 Bumrah captained India in the fifth Test against England, finishing that campaign as player of the series with 23 wickets.

The unorthodox bowler was massive during India’s 2023 ODI World Cup run and 2024 T20 World Cup success, named player of the series in the latter for his 15 wickets at 8.26 and 2-18 in the final.
